question.problem:
Suppose $a=[4,\,6]^{T}$ and $b=[2,\,-2]^{T}.$ Find the Euclidean distance between $a$ and $b.$

Rounded to three decimal places, ${d}_{2}(a,b)≈$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Euclidean distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{2}(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{2}
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{2}=\sqrt{{\sum }_{i=1}^{N}|{v}_{i}{|}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{2}(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{2} \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]‖}_{2} \\  & =\sqrt{|4-2{|}^{2}+|6-(-2){|}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{68} \\  & ≈8.246.\end{aligned}
$$
